British Values
Turnham Academy understands the importance of British Values and we have ensured our curriculum promotes our pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
We strongly believe our British Values are promoted in all aspects of school life and sit at the heart of our diverse and inclusive community.
The five British Values that our form part of the learning for pupils at Turnham are:
Tolerance of other faiths and beliefs.
We ensure the fundamental British Values are embedded within our curriculum and subjects, to further develop understanding of these concepts through; Philosophy for Children (P4C), Relationship Sex Education (RSE), Religious Education (RE), assemblies and Pupil Parliament.

Welcome from the Regional Director
Welcome to Turnham Academy
On behalf of the children and staff, it is with pleasure that I welcome you to Turnham Academy. We are extremely proud of the strong values, educational achievements and the opportunities our children receive throughout their educational journey.
We place learners at the heart of everything and through our rich and ambitious curriculum, children learn in a safe and stimulating environment.
We pride ourselves in supporting all children to become life-long learners and successful adults in the modern World because of the strong foundations built from the moment children enter into our academy.
Turnham Academy values our diverse community and is committed to ensuring equity and inclusion for all children.
Our strong partnerships with other excellent academies in STEP, enables us to work together to strive for excellence.
As you navigate through our website, you will see passionate, confident and independent learners. We look forward to meeting you and showing you around our academy so please book a visit.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head Teacher
Welcome to Turnham Academy
We are a thriving, vibrant, multi-cultural primary school at the heart of our community in Brockley, in the London Borough of Lewisham.
Our pupils are kind, happy and respectful and love coming to school every day. Our dedicated staffing team will work in partnership with you to ensure that we give your child the education that they truly deserve.
Our school values are Passion, Urgency, Positivity, Aspiration and Commitment. We use these to ensure that we provide the best for our pupils, staff and community always.
Our 3 curriculum drivers are Collaboration, Curiosity and Communication.
We teach our pupils to work as a team and be equipped with the social skills to enable them to be successful throughout their education and beyond. Our pupils are passionate lifelong learners with a thirst for finding out more.
We excite and engage our pupils through carefully crafted learning opportunities, experiences and educational visits. We believe that our pupils can make a positive impact on the community, their country and their world.
We equip our pupils with the tools to be effective communicators who present themselves with confidence. We value pupil voice and actively encourage our children in their right to be heard.
We provide all who attend Turnham Academy with the opportunity to achieve anything that they want to in life.
Our fantastic, modern facilities are second to none. Turnham Academy has beautiful, spacious playgrounds, forest school facilities, dedicated Art , DT and music rooms, a world class library and our 3G football pitch, “The Rocky and Wrighty Arena”, recently opened by our ex pupil, star Arsenal and England striker Ian Wright.
Contact the Academy office to book a tour and see how Turnham Academy will enable your child to reach their full potential.

Art & DT
At Turnham Academy, we believe that a high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design. As pupils progress, they should be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design from around the world. They should also know how art and design both reflect and shape our history, and contribute to the culture, creativity and wealth of our world.
The purpose of education is to develop well-rounded, knowledgeable individuals who are prepared to contribute meaningfully to society. Design and Technology (DT) at Turnham Academy supports this aim by introducing pupils to the big ideas of the subject where they will learn critically evaluate the impact of technologies and products on daily life and the wider world, fostering a sense of responsibility and stewardship toward the environment and society. This approach demands that 'pupils develop the creative, technical and practical expertise needed to perform everyday tasks confidently and to participate successfully in an increasingly technological world.' (Department for Education, 2013).
A core aspect of the curriculum is to provide pupils contexts from which they need to apply their learning from other disciplines. Pupils should be drawing from disciplines such as mathematics, science, computing, and art while considering how this knowledge can be incorporated into the big ideas of DT: Knowledge of materials, manufacturing, functionality, design and critique. The fusion of these disciplines must be considered through the contexts of their own and others' needs, wants, and values so that they can successfully generate, develop, and communicate design ideas, evaluate their own work and that of others, and understand the principles of nutrition and healthy eating.
Aspirational in content, the curriculum aligns with the English National Curriculum and the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework. The skills learned are invaluable not only for academic success but also for personal growth in an ever-increasing technological world.

History & Geography
We want our pupils to develop into historians who have an understanding of present and past conditions of all people.
Our aim is to develop pupils so that they are able to do the following :
• Have an excellent knowledge and understanding of people, events and places from different historical periods, both in Britain and the wider world.
• Understand the chronology of time and place which underpins their sense of different periods and allows them to consider change and causation.
• Think critically about history and communicating these ideas to a variety of audiences.
• Have the ability to support, evaluate and challenge their own and others opinions when using historical evidence from a range of sources.
• Formulate questions and apply a line of enquiry in order to present, analyse and reflect on what they find.
• Be curious and have a genuine interest pertaining to the past and its people.
We want our pupils to develop into active, responsible citizens, who have curiosity pertaining to the world and their local area. We allow opportunities for investigations and enquiry and develop their communication skills so that they can share their findings in various ways to a range of audiences.
Our aim is to develop pupils so that they are able to do the following :
• Have an excellent knowledge of places both in Britain and the wider world and the vocabulary with which to describe them.
• Have a comprehensive understanding of the ways in which places are interdependent and interconnected
• Think critically about society and environmental issues while bearing in mind bias and alternative opinions
• Formulate questions and apply a line of enquiry in order to present, analyse and reflect on what they find
• Have adept field work skills and other geographical skills

Music
Music is a vehicle for self-expression, motivation, inspiration and a path to a healthy mental wellbeing, therefore at Turnham Academy we understand that music plays a vital role in a child’s life. Our aim is to provide a framework based on the National Curriculum to ensure that all pupils be taught to sing, create and compose music, have opportunities to perform, listen, review and evaluate, and to develop their musical skills, knowledge and understanding.
With the support of the external provider Rhythm Connections, we aim to help children to sing and use their voices, create and compose music, have the opportunity to learn a musical instrument, use technology appropriately and have the opportunity to progress to the next level in musical excellence. We aim to give children a greater awareness of the range of music and musical activities through events within and outside of school in order for them to leave primary school with a well rounded musical education.

Year 6 go surfing
On Friday 13th June Year 6 travelled to Joss Bay in Broadstairs, Kent to spend a day surfing in the sunshine.
In association with the charity GET OUT and Joss Bay Surf School, the pupils learned how to surf, whislt also being taught about the importance of looking after the sea.
They learned about the amount of rubbish that enters the ocean every day and how they can play a part in ensuring that the beaches and seas are clean and safe for all to enjoy.

Physical Education
“Sana mens in corpore sano” (a healthy mind in a healthy body), Juvenal
We believe a physically literate child is a competent, confident and healthy mover. Physical literacy builds motivation, confidence, physical competence and an understanding of movement. Thus, it provides our children with the strong foundations needed to sustain a lifelong participation in physical activity and sport. Our children benefit from a broad and balanced Physical Education (PE) programme carefully designed to inspire learners to:
· become physically literate and confident in a way which supports their health and fitness
· be physically active for sustained periods of time
· engage in competitive sports and activities that build character and help to embed values
· succeed and excel in physical activities and sport
· discover skills, abilities and preferences, and make choices about how to get involved lifelong physical activity
Physical Literacy is reinforced through daily active playtimes and our extensive extra-curricular and competitive school sport programme.

Reception
At Turnham Academy, we believe that all children deserve an education rich in wonder and memorable experiences that allows children's natural creativity and curiosity to flourish alongside the purposeful acquisition of skills and knowledge.
We believe that an education that does all of this allows all children to reach their personal goals and fulfil their potential. We know that our children enter our Reception classes with varied life experiences, and we aim to plan teaching and learning opportunities accordingly to address this.
At Turnham Academy, we work closely with parents, carers and other settings to provide every child with the best possible start, ensuring each individual reaches their full potential from various starting points. We recognise the crucial role that Early Years education plays in providing firm foundations upon which the rest of a child’s education is successfully based. Therefore, we provide an engaging, progressive curriculum that maximises opportunities for meaningful cross-curricular links and learning experiences and promotes the unique child by offering extended periods of play and sustained thinking.

Science
At Turnham Academy, we believe that the purpose of science education is to equip children with the foundational knowledge and skills they need to understand the world. In science, we serve this purpose by fostering curiosity and teaching the substantive knowledge of biology, chemistry, and physics. This is underpinned by disciplinary knowledge, where working scientifically is developed through rigorous practice and reasoning. From the Early Years Foundation Stage, pupils begin building their scientific understanding, exploring the world around them and acquiring vocabulary that is explicitly taught to ensure clarity and precision in communication.
Our curriculum is aligned to the National Curriculum for science and the EYFS statutory framework, providing aspirational content that progressively deepens pupils' knowledge. We prioritise core concepts, ensuring that all learning is rooted in a strong scientific foundation, which supports practical investigations and critical thinking. Cross-curricular links to mathematics, geography, design and technology, physical education, and PSHE enrich the learning experience and show how science is interwoven with everyday life.
By maintaining high expectations and fostering a love for learning, our curriculum ensures that pupils leave primary school with the scientific literacy necessary for future academic success and informed citizenship.

Computing
When planning and teaching Computing at Turnham Academy, we believe that it is an essential part of the curriculum; a subject that not only stands alone but is woven in and should be an integral part of all learning. Computing, in general, is a significant part of everyone’s daily life and children should be at the forefront of new technology, with a thirst for learning what is out there.
Computing within schools can therefore provide a wealth of learning opportunities and transferable skills explicitly within the Computing lesson and across other curriculum subjects. Through the study of Computing, children will be able to develop a wide range of fundamental skills, knowledge and understanding that will actually equip them for the rest of their life.
Computers and technology are such a part of everyday life that our children would be at a disadvantage would they not be exposed to a thorough and robust Computing curriculum. Children must be taught in the art form of ‘Computational Thinking’ in order to provide them essential knowledge that will enable them to participate effectively and safely in the digital world beyond our gates.

English
Reading
Our English approach is a reading and writing programme devised to accelerate and challenge children’s reading and writing abilities. It initially lays strong foundations in both oracy and English with Nursery and Reception children and goes on to provide systematic teaching throughout the primary years. This provides a wide range of opportunities for children to explore and develop phonic knowledge and comprehension strategies; develop vocabulary and spelling; improve grammatical awareness; analyse whole texts; and develop writing in a range of genres, all whilst exposing children to a wide range of interesting, bright and diverse range of literature.

Spanish
The purpose of education is to develop well-rounded, knowledgeable individuals who are prepared to contribute meaningfully to society. Foreign Languages education at Turnham Academy supports this aim by fostering an appreciation for cultural diversity and promoting intercultural understanding through the engagement of authentic materials, such as songs, poems, and cultural traditions, which enrich their personal development and equip them with the emotional intelligence and cross-cultural competencies vital for thriving in a multicultural world.
As novice learners, pupils will focus on the fundamental building blocks of language acquisition: phonics, vocabulary, and grammar. Initially, they will prioritise listening and speaking, progressing to reading and writing. By using high-utility vocabulary, pupils will learn to construct coherent sentences. Our curriculum is aspirational yet accessible, providing a clear and structured pathway that aligns with the English National Curriculum's Key Stage 2 framework.
This approach nurtures curiosity, resilience, and a love for languages, ensuring that all pupils, regardless of background, have the foundation to succeed in further language study and confidently navigate an interconnected world.
